title: Compiler directives (#if, #nullable, #region)
hook: C# compiler directives are switches the compiler reads before building your code. They are not a separate C preprocessor and they are not regular if statements — #if removes code entirely, while #nullable toggles static analysis warnings.

blocks.text: A **compiler directive** starts with `#` and instructs the C# compiler to include, exclude, or annotate code before compilation finishes. `#if` / `#elif` / `#else` / `#endif` conditionally include code based on defined symbols like DEBUG. `#nullable` toggles nullable reference type analysis. `#region` / `#endregion` are editor folding markers with zero run-time effect. These are fundamentally different from regular if statements — `#if` strips tokens before the compiler even sees them.

entries.plainDefinition: Includes or excludes code blocks based on whether a compile-time symbol is defined. The excluded code is not compiled at all.
entries.example: #if DEBUG ... #endif — only present in Debug builds.

entries.plainDefinition: Toggles nullable reference type (NRT) analysis for the following code. Does not change how string is stored at run time.
entries.example: #nullable enable makes the compiler warn when you assign null to a non-nullable string.

entries.plainDefinition: A C# feature that uses ? annotations and compiler warnings to catch null reference bugs before run time. Full rules are in module 07.
entries.example: string? means the variable may be null; string means the compiler expects it never to be.

sections.heading: Why directives are not if statements

blocks.text: A regular if runs at run time and both branches are compiled. An #if runs at compile time and the false branch does not exist in the output assembly. Use #if for diagnostic-only logging in a RabbitMQ publisher, not for swapping entire implementations — that belongs in Dependency Injection (DI). #region is for editor folding only; it is not architecture. File-based #: directives in .NET 10 apps are SDK configuration, not this preprocessor set.

blocks.title: Where to define symbols
blocks.body: Define DEBUG and TRACE at the project level via the .csproj or dotnet build -c Debug. You can also write #define TRACE at the top of a single file, but project-level constants are easier to manage.

items.title: Read directives
items.body: The compiler scans for # lines before parsing regular code.

items.title: Evaluate conditions
items.body: #if checks whether a symbol like DEBUG is defined in the current build configuration.

items.title: Strip or keep tokens
items.body: Code in false branches is removed entirely — it is not dead code, it does not exist.

items.title: Apply nullable context
items.body: #nullable enable turns on warnings for the following lines until #nullable restore or disable.

diagram.title: #if versus regular if
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[Source code] --> B{#if DEBUG?}
  B -->|Symbol defined| C[Keep debug code in compilation]
  B -->|Symbol not defined| D[Remove debug code entirely]
  C --> E[Compile remaining tokens]
  D --> E
  E --> F[Run-time: no if check needed for stripped code]

snippet.label: Conditional compile versus nullable switch
snippet.explanation: #if strips code from the compilation. #nullable only changes static analysis warnings. Do not mix them in your head.

snippet.label: #elif, #else, and #warning
snippet.explanation: #elif and #else work like you expect at compile time. #warning emits a compiler warning; #error blocks compilation entirely.

snippet.label: #pragma warning and scoped disable
snippet.explanation: Scope #pragma warning disable to the smallest region possible. Disabling nullable at file scope to silence warnings is a smell — fix the types.

blocks.title: Top pitfalls
blocks.body: Shipping a #if DEBUG security bypass that is off in Release — still a design smell. Disabling nullable at file scope to silence warnings instead of fixing types. Confusing #: file-based directives with #if preprocessor directives. Using #region as a substitute for proper class decomposition.

interviewTakeaways: #if removes tokens before bind; it is not an if statement.
#nullable is an analyzer/compiler switch; full Nullable Reference Type (NRT) rules are module 07.
#region is editor folding only — not architecture.
#: directives in file-based apps are SDK config, not preprocessor directives.
commonPitfalls: Shipping a #if DEBUG security bypass that is off in Release — still a design smell.
Disabling nullable at file scope to silence warnings instead of fixing types.
Treating #region as a design tool instead of editor convenience.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript has no #if. Bundlers drop unused modules; C# #if drops tokens before compile. TypeScript /// <reference> is a different kind of directive.
